The same-run two-phone access-VLAN control.  One disposable, one window: the control phone kept access 931 / voice 930 and the intervention phone's port carried access 930 / voice 930, with every other action identical.  Primary outcome did not move -- both phones DHCP-armed, no address, 0 bindings, NOT_REGISTERED -- but the voice-VLAN STP membership DID: the control port stays ABSENT from the VLAN0930 instance exactly as runs 3-8, while the intervention port appears in it, LIS before the window and LRN after it.  FWD was not observed at either snapshot; that the port never reached FWD at some unread moment inside the window is NOT established -- two snapshots do not prove every intermediate state.  The access-VLAN shape controls voice-VLAN spanning-tree membership on this build; whether a port OBSERVED forwarding also leases is exactly what this run could not answer.  The follow-up is the FWD-gated fresh-DHCP rerun under natural convergence: arm only after a qualified read observes FWD, and only when the pre-arm readback proves a real OFF-to-ON trigger.

RUN12 observational phone DHCP lifecycle qualification. The intervention VLAN930 gate observed LIS -> LRN -> UNOBSERVABLE(COMPLETENESS) -> LRN -> UNOBSERVABLE(COMPLETENESS) -> FORWARDING across 15 samples / 31171 ms; the terminal sample was authoritative. For both P1 control and P2 intervention, SVI DHCP was first observed YES at IMMEDIATELY_BEFORE_STP_FWD_GATE and was already YES before authoritative FWD. Device-level DHCP was UNOBSERVABLE at every retained milestone, so its first YES was NOT_ESTABLISHED and enabled-before-FWD was UNOBSERVABLE. Neither SVI nor device IPv4 appeared at any milestone. The enabled flag does not establish Discover, DORA, retry, transaction progress, or milestone causation; sequential reads may shift later observation time slightly. Realtime and the empty semantic workspace were restored with zero errors; no rerun occurred.
